I left `src/parse.ts` unchanged, because the contract for this spec is already in it.

- **Nothing to add:** the spec says "No export is added, removed or renamed, and no signature changes." Every export it lists is already in `src/parse.ts` with that exact signature: `parseURL`, `parsePath`, `parseAuth`, `parseHost`, `stringifyParsedURL`, `parseFilename`, `ParsedURL`, `ParsedAuth` and `ParsedHost`. The spec names no new constant, type or parameter, and no error.
- **What changes is behaviour, and that belongs to the implementer:** `parseURL` should remove the slash before a drive letter only when the protocol written in the input is exactly `file:`. Making that change means editing the body of `parseURL`, and your rules say existing bodies must stay as they are, so I didn't touch it.
- **Both test suites can already import what they need:** `parseURL`, `parseFilename` and `stringifyParsedURL` from `src/index.ts`, with the existing `ParsedURL` type. No test-controlled inputs such as time, keys or randomness are involved.

`npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors, and `npx vitest run` passes as before (13 files, 467 tests).

Exported names added: none.

public.finalText:
I wrote the test suite in `test/ufo-drive-letters-check.test.ts`. Type-checking passes: `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors. That project's config only includes `src`, so I also type-checked the test file on its own, and it was clean too.

**One difference from what you described:** `src/parse.ts` does not throw `not implemented`. It still has the old code, which removes the slash before a drive letter for every protocol. So the run is mixed, not all-failing: **22 fail, 36 pass**.

- **The 22 failures** are the tests for the new behaviour, which the old code doesn't have yet: `FILE:`/`File:` not being normalized, `///C:/foo`, `http:`/`https:`/`ftp:`/`s3:` paths keeping their slash, the `http:` round-trip and `parseFilename` cases, and `defaultProto` set to `http://` or `FILE://`.
- **The 36 passes** cover behaviour that stays the same: `file:` URLs being normalized, the backslash and whitespace inputs, the single-letter drive rule, the unanchored single-match pattern, plain paths, and `blob:`/`data:` URLs.

**How the tests are built:**
- Every scenario has its own key, from `[happy-1]` to `[happy-4]`, `[boundary-1]` to `[boundary-11]`, and `[unhappy-1]` to `[unhappy-3]`, counted in spec order.
- Each example row of a Scenario Outline is its own test. The tests are flat top-level `test` calls, built in loops the way `test/parse.test.ts` does it.
- Each scenario also gets one extra boundary test that follows directly from the spec's rules. Examples: `fILE:///C:/foo`, `files://host/C:/x`, a non-ASCII letter before `:`, `/C:/foo` with `defaultProto` set to `FILE://`, and `http://host/C:` giving the filename `C:`.
- Results are compared as in the existing tests, through a JSON round-trip. Tests use `toEqual` where the spec says "the result equals" and `toMatchObject` where it lists only some fields.
- Imports come from `../src/parse`, as you asked, not from `src/index.ts` as the spec's Background says.

58 tests, in 1 file.

private.finalText:
I wrote the hidden suite as two files in `test/hidden-ufo-drive-letters-check/`. `tsc` reports no errors. The rule that every test must fail against the code as it stands can't be fully met, though: `src/parse.ts` was never stubbed.

**The seam still has the old code.** `parseURL` still contains the old implementation, which removes the slash before a drive letter for every protocol. Nothing in it throws `not implemented`. So:
- **58 tests fail** against the current code, as intended. These are other protocols, protocol-relative inputs, uppercase `FILE:`, `defaultProto http://`, the stringify round-trip and `parseFilename`.
- **67 tests pass** against the current code. They cover behaviour the spec says stays the same: lowercase `file:` normalization, plain paths, `//C:/foo`, the single-match unanchored pattern, and `blob:`/`javascript:`. No correct test of those scenarios can fail against code that already does the right thing. I kept them because they stop an implementation from breaking that behaviour.

**Checks I ran in a scratch copy of the repo:**
- **Reference implementation:** I patched in a minimal version of the spec (remove the slash only when `protocol === "file:"`). All 125 hidden tests, the 58 public tests and `test/parse.test.ts` pass against it.
- **Shortcut mutants:** each of these passes all 58 public tests, and the hidden suite fails it:

| Shortcut | Hidden tests failed | Caught by |
|---|---|---|
| `input.trim().startsWith("file:")` | 1 | leading `\0` |
| `input.includes("file:")` | 3 | `http://host/file:/C:/x?file:/D:/y` |
| `[A-z]` instead of `[A-Za-z]` | 3 | `[:`, `_:`, `` `: `` |
| case-insensitive Unicode regex `/[a-z]:/iu` | 2 | Kelvin sign U+212A, long s U+017F |
| `protocol.endsWith("file:")` | 2 | `myfile:`, `afile:` |
| anchored `^\/+` | 10 | slash deep in the path, `file:////C:/x` |

Other cases target the remaining shortcuts:
- normalizing only when the host is empty: hosts with auth and port;
- normalizing the pathname only: matches in search and hash;
- a global replace: three drive-letter candidates;
- using `defaultProto` as the protocol to check: `///C:/foo` with `file://`;
- trimming whitespace before a case-insensitive check: `  FILE:///`.

125 tests, in 2 files.

Open in the spec: none
